behavioral_effects: Six bounded views render as offline self-contained HTML from graph slices: architecture, site, impact, configuration, migration, security - driven by governance/views/definitions.json and the new make governance-visualize target. The site map was verified in the browser: pages, proxy handlers, backend modules in columns with the WS bypass drawn as its own edge.
Truncation is drawn on the page itself with the focus hint, so a bounded view can never read as a complete one.
compatibility_impact: None breaking. governance visualize leaves deferred status; its exit-2 stub becomes the real command, which is the promised direction of that contract. definitions.json is curated with a kernel-internal schema.
follow_up: Session 7.4 wires the advisory policy entries, updates the agent surface, and writes the phase-7 exit measurement.
limitations: Layout is layered columns, not force-directed: right for flows and maps, weak for dense meshes - the migration chain reads better in its edge list than its picture.
reason: Every graph answer is text in a terminal: reviewers judging a change still have no picture of the chain it crosses or the neighborhood it lands in, which is the exact phase-7 trigger the blueprint names; this defines the bounded views as governed data, renders them as self-contained HTML from graph slices, and turns the deferred visualize stub into the real command
risks: The views read committed manifests; a stale manifest renders a stale picture - the drift checks that guard the manifests are the mitigation.
rollback: git revert of the single commit; artifacts/governance pages are regenerable litter, not state.
security_impact: Rendered pages are self-contained HTML with no scripts and no external requests, pinned by test; the security view draws the permission map and its notes carry the three standing MCP findings rather than hiding them. artifacts/ is gitignored, verified before writing.
summary: Build the bounded views and un-defer governance visualize
